subject: Maximum penalized likelihood estimation in unmarked ?

messages.author: 0757c7f287cc9bab
messages.subject: Maximum penalized likelihood estimation in unmarked ?
parts:
Hi, everyone
I have several questions about the maximum penalized likelihood estimations (MPLE):
1. My camera-trap survey sample size is small ( for each analysis, only about 40-50 sites, each site has 45 or 77 camera-days depending on different seasons), and the detection probabilities are low (naive detection probabilities range from 0.01 to 0.11 for different species/season combinations). Therefore when I used the ordinary single-season occupancy model to fit the data, I got large SE of the occupancy factor coefficients and "boundary estimates" of the occupancy probabilities (i.e. all the grids' occupancy probabilities were near 1 or 0). Thus I would like to follow Monica Moreno & Subhash R. Lele (2010) and Rebecca A. Hutchinson et al. (2015) to use MPLE. I would like to choose the logistic regression penalty which is recommended by Monica Moreno & Subhash R. Lele (2010), but I wonder your expert opinions on whether it is reasonable to use the logistic regression result to counterbalance the occupancy analysis result?
2. Is there any way to conduct the MPLE by unmarked ? The Monica Moreno & Subhash R. Lele (2010) paper said they had released their R code online, but I didn't find it in the linked website. The Rebecca A. Hutchinson et al. (2015) paper also said the MPLE methods would be included in the next release of unmarked, but I failed to find the MPLE command in unmarked or other R packages.
3. Is it reasonable to use MPLE to fit Royal-Nichol model ? If so, whether we should introduce a factor describing site abundance into the logistic regression penalty ?
Look forward to your suggestions:) Thanks a lot !
Best wishes,
Sun, Ge

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Maximum penalized likelihood estimation in unmarked ?
parts:
Dear Sun,
 1. I don't have any specific input on this one
 2. The next release of unmarked (later this summer) should have the Hutchinson et al. (2015) in it.  I will see if I can send you a special version of unmarked to use which has this but it might be a couple days before I can look into it.
 3. I don't know if it's reasonable or not, but unmarked will not have that capabilitiy.

regards
andy
